Questions.QuestionText: Which keyword is used in C# to automatically call Dispose() on an IDisposable object when exiting scope?
Options: using
dispose
finalize
auto
Questions.Explanation: The 'using' statement defines a scope at the end of which the IDisposable object will be automatically disposed.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary difference between a struct (value type) and a class (reference type) in C#?
Options: Structs are allocated on the stack (or inline) and copied by value; classes are heap-allocated and copied by reference
Structs support inheritance while classes do not
Classes cannot implement interfaces
Structs can have parameterless constructors prior to C# 10
Questions.Explanation: Structs are value types allocated on the stack/inline and passed by value, whereas classes are reference types allocated on the managed heap.

Questions.QuestionText: Which of the following creates an immutable record type with positional properties in modern C#?
Options: public record Person(string FirstName, string LastName);
public struct Person { string FirstName; string LastName; }
public static class Person(string FirstName, string LastName);
public interface Person(string FirstName, string LastName);
Questions.Explanation: Positional record syntax generates an immutable reference type with init-only properties and value-based equality.

Questions.QuestionText: How do async/await methods handle synchronization and non-blocking I/O in .NET?
Options: By creating a state machine that yields execution back to the caller/threadpool without blocking the calling thread
By running synchronous operations in a background task loop indefinitely
By using Thread.Sleep until the operation completes
By pausing all other threads in the process
Questions.Explanation: The compiler transforms async methods into a state machine that registers continuations without blocking threads during I/O waits.

Questions.QuestionText: Which collection type provides lock-free or lightweight thread-safe operations in System.Collections.Concurrent?
Options: ConcurrentDictionary<TKey, TValue>
List<T>
Dictionary<TKey, TValue>
HashSet<T>
Questions.Explanation: ConcurrentDictionary is specifically designed for thread-safe operations without requiring manual locking.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the lifetime of a service registered with AddScoped in the ASP.NET Core Dependency Injection container?
Options: Created once per HTTP request and shared across components handling that request
Created once for the entire application lifetime
Created every time the service is requested
Created once per user session
Questions.Explanation: Scoped services are created once per client request scope and disposed when the HTTP request ends.

Questions.QuestionText: In ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline execution, what is the purpose of the 'next' delegate?
Options: To invoke the next middleware component in the pipeline
To abort the request immediately
To restart the pipeline from the beginning
To authenticate the incoming HTTP headers
Questions.Explanation: Calling await next(context) passes execution to the next middleware in the HTTP request pipeline.

Questions.QuestionText: Which filter or attribute is used to protect ASP.NET Core POST actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)?
Options: [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] / [AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken]
[Authorize]
[AllowAnonymous]
[ResponseCache]
Questions.Explanation: [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] validates the incoming antiforgery request token header or form field.

Questions.QuestionText: How does ASP.NET Core handle static files (e.g. CSS, JS, images) by default?
Options: Through app.UseStaticFiles() serving files out of wwwroot
Automatically through routing without any middleware
Through EF Core database queries
By streaming them through the Razor view engine
Questions.Explanation: app.UseStaticFiles() enables serving static assets located in the wwwroot web root folder.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary benefit of Tag Helpers in Razor Views?
Options: They enable server-side code to participate in creating and rendering HTML elements in Razor files in an HTML-friendly syntax
They replace JavaScript on the client side
They automatically translate English text into other languages
They bypass database queries
Questions.Explanation: Tag Helpers allow server-side C# logic to augment HTML tags with clean, idiomatic HTML syntax (e.g. asp-action, asp-for).

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary distinction between a Clustered Index and a Non-Clustered Index in SQL Server?
Options: A Clustered index physically sorts and stores data rows at leaf level (only one per table); Non-Clustered contains row pointers
A table can have multiple clustered indexes but only one non-clustered index
Clustered indexes cannot be used for primary keys
Non-clustered indexes replace table storage completely
Questions.Explanation: A clustered index defines the physical order of data in the table, so only one can exist per table.

Questions.QuestionText: Which SQL Server feature provides tokenization, word-breaking, and linguistic stemming for searching text columns?
Options: Full-Text Search (FTS) with CONTAINS / CONTAINSTABLE
Scalar LIKE queries
Partitioned views
Columnstore indexing
Questions.Explanation: SQL Server Full-Text Search builds inverted word catalogs supporting prefix and proximity queries via CONTAINS/CONTAINSTABLE.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the SQL error code 2601 or 2627 signify in SQL Server?
Options: Violation of UNIQUE KEY or PRIMARY KEY constraint (duplicate key insertion)
Foreign key constraint violation
Check constraint failure
Timeout expired while executing query
Questions.Explanation: Error 2601/2627 indicates an attempt to insert a duplicate value into a column with a UNIQUE index or primary key.

Questions.QuestionText: Why is parameterized SQL mandatory when building database queries with dynamic user inputs?
Options: It prevents SQL Injection attacks and allows the query optimizer to reuse cached execution plans
It automatically compiles SQL queries to C# bytecode
It removes the need for database indexes
It compresses the database files on disk
Questions.Explanation: Parameterization treats input strictly as literal values rather than executable code, stopping SQL injection and enabling plan caching.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the effect of the READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT isolation level (RCSI) in SQL Server?
Options: Readers do not block writers and writers do not block readers by using row versioning in tempdb
It locks all read tables exclusively until transaction completion
It allows dirty reads of uncommitted data
It turns off transaction logging
Questions.Explanation: RCSI uses row versioning in tempdb to provide snapshot consistency so read queries never block concurrent write operations.

Questions.QuestionText: When should AsNoTracking() be applied to EF Core queries?
Options: For read-only queries where entities will not be modified or saved back to the database
When performing entity updates or deletes
When creating database migrations
Only when using in-memory mock databases
Questions.Explanation: AsNoTracking() turns off change tracking snapshot overhead, significantly reducing memory consumption and improving read query performance.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of FromSql / FromSqlRaw in EF Core?
Options: To execute hand-written, parameterized raw SQL queries while mapping results to EF entities or models
To generate automatic EF migrations
To export database tables to JSON
To format dates in SQL syntax
Questions.Explanation: FromSql and FromSqlRaw allow developers to execute hand-authored SQL statements with full control over query design and performance.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the N+1 query problem and how does Eager Loading (.Include()) resolve it?
Options: N+1 occurs when navigating navigation properties causes separate queries per parent row; .Include() issues a JOIN in one query
N+1 refers to having N database servers plus one load balancer
N+1 means adding one column to N tables simultaneously
It is resolved by disabling foreign keys
Questions.Explanation: Include() eagerly joins and fetches child records in a single database round-trip rather than making N individual roundtrips.

Questions.QuestionText: Which method on DbContext persists all tracked changes to the underlying database within an automatic transaction?
Options: SaveChangesAsync()
CommitTransaction()
FlushChanges()
SyncDatabase()
Questions.Explanation: SaveChangesAsync() writes all inserted, updated, and deleted entities tracked by the ChangeTracker to the database.

Questions.QuestionText: How can EF Core execute arbitrary raw non-query SQL (such as an INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE) asynchronously?
Options: await db.Database.ExecuteSqlRawAsync(sql, parameters, ct)
await db.Database.RunAsync(sql)
await db.ExecuteBatch(sql)
await db.QueryRawAsync(sql)
Questions.Explanation: Database.ExecuteSqlRawAsync executes raw commands against the database connection and returns the number of affected rows.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the difference between '==' and '===' in JavaScript?
Options: '===' performs strict equality checking without type coercion; '==' coerces operands of different types
'==' compares memory addresses while '===' compares values
'===' is only used for strings and '==' is used for numbers
There is no functional difference
Questions.Explanation: The strict equality operator === verifies both value and type without converting types.

Questions.QuestionText: How does the JavaScript Event Loop handle asynchronous promises (microtasks) compared to setTimeout (macrotasks)?
Options: Microtasks (Promise callbacks) are drained completely before the next macrotask (setTimeout) is processed
Macrotasks have higher priority than microtasks
Microtasks only run when the browser tab loses focus
They run in parallel on background worker threads
Questions.Explanation: The microtask queue (Promises, queueMicrotask) is processed immediately after the current task and before the next macrotask.

Questions.QuestionText: What is a Closure in JavaScript?
Options: A function bundled together with references to its surrounding lexical environment
A syntax for closing browser windows
A method to delete variables from memory
An HTML tag closing bracket
Questions.Explanation: A closure gives an inner function access to its outer enclosing scope even after the outer function has executed.

Questions.QuestionText: Which native API is modern JavaScript standard for sending asynchronous HTTP requests?
Options: fetch()
XMLHttpRequest (XHR)
$.ajax()
http.get()
Questions.Explanation: fetch() is the standard promise-based browser API for making network requests.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the JavaScript method Array.prototype.reduce() do?
Options: Executes a user-supplied reducer callback function on each element of the array, resulting in a single accumulated output value
Shrinks the length of the array by half
Deletes empty elements from the array
Sorts the array in descending order
Questions.Explanation: reduce() iterates through an array and accumulates the elements into a single accumulated result.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary rule when using React Hooks (e.g. useState, useEffect)?
Options: Hooks must only be called at the top level of React function components or custom hooks, never inside loops, conditions, or nested functions
Hooks must always be called inside class components
Hooks can only be called inside setTimeout callbacks
Hooks must be called after return statements
Questions.Explanation: React relies on the call order of hooks across re-renders, so they must always be executed unconditionally at the top level.

Questions.QuestionText: Why is it important to provide a unique 'key' prop when rendering lists in React?
Options: Keys help React identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed during Virtual DOM reconciliation
Keys encrypt the data in the browser
Keys format CSS classes automatically
Keys prevent the component from re-rendering
Questions.Explanation: Keys give elements a stable identity so React can efficiently match and patch Virtual DOM nodes rather than re-creating them.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the dependency array in useEffect([dependencies]) control?
Options: When the effect function re-runs: if empty ([]), runs once on mount; if omitted, runs on every render; if populated, runs when dependencies change
It specifies which CSS stylesheets to load
It defines which child components to render
It acts as a database connection pool
Questions.Explanation: The dependency array tells React to skip running the effect unless one of the listed values has changed between renders.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of React.memo()?
Options: A higher-order component that memoizes the rendered output and skips re-rendering if props have not changed (shallow comparison)
A hook to store global variables in local storage
A tool to remember browser history
A debugger for React Native
Questions.Explanation: React.memo prevents unnecessary re-renders of functional components when the incoming props remain shallowly identical.

Questions.QuestionText: How does React state updates behave with useState?
Options: State updates are asynchronous and batched; mutating state directly does not trigger a re-render
State updates are synchronous and mutate the variable directly
State cannot hold objects or arrays
State is shared automatically across all components
Questions.Explanation: React batches state updates and requires calling the setter function with a new reference to trigger reconciliation.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary difference between a Docker Image and a Docker Container?
Options: An image is an immutable, read-only template; a container is a running, stateful instance of an image
A container contains the source code while an image contains only documentation
Images require VirtualBox while containers run on bare metal
There is no difference between them
Questions.Explanation: A Docker image is a packaged static blueprint, while a container is a live, running instantiation of that blueprint.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the benefit of multi-stage builds in a Dockerfile?
Options: They separate the build environment (SDKs/compilers) from the final lean runtime image, keeping production image size small
They allow running multiple operating systems inside a single container simultaneously
They bypass container security checks
They increase image build time without changing output size
Questions.Explanation: Multi-stage builds leave behind intermediate build tools and SDKs, copying only final build artifacts into a minimal runtime image.

Questions.QuestionText: What Docker mechanism is used to persist data generated by and used by Docker containers beyond their lifecycle?
Options: Docker Volumes / Bind Mounts
Container RAM caches
Environment variables
Dockerfile RUN commands
Questions.Explanation: Volumes are managed by Docker and store persistent data outside the container's temporary writable layer.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the function of the EXPOSE instruction in a Dockerfile?
Options: It acts as documentation indicating which port the container listens on at runtime (port mapping -p is still needed to publish)
It opens the firewall for all incoming internet traffic automatically
It publishes ports to the host without any run flags
It exposes the root password of the container
Questions.Explanation: EXPOSE informs Docker that the container listens on specific ports, but does not publish them without -p or -P at runtime.

Questions.QuestionText: What does 'docker compose up -d' do?
Options: Builds, creates, and starts all services defined in docker-compose.yml in the background (detached mode)
Deletes all stopped containers and unused images
Upgrades Docker daemon to the latest version
Downloads Docker Desktop installer
Questions.Explanation: docker compose up starts all defined services, and -d specifies detached mode so the shell remains free.

Questions.QuestionText: What does Idempotency mean in the context of HTTP methods?
Options: Making multiple identical requests has the same intended effect on the server as making a single request (e.g. GET, PUT, DELETE)
The method returns data in encrypted format
The endpoint requires user authentication
The request cannot be cached by intermediate proxies
Questions.Explanation: An idempotent HTTP method produces the same resource state regardless of how many times it is repeated.

Questions.QuestionText: Which HTTP status code should be returned when a request is well-formed but conflicts with the current state of the resource (e.g. duplicate key)?
Options: 409 Conflict
400 Bad Request
404 Not Found
500 Internal Server Error
Questions.Explanation: HTTP 409 Conflict indicates that the request cannot be completed due to a conflict with current server state (such as a unique constraint violation).

Questions.QuestionText: What is the recommended HTTP method for partially updating an existing resource?
Options: PATCH
PUT
POST
GET
Questions.Explanation: PATCH applies partial modifications to a resource, whereas PUT typically replaces the entire resource representation.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of the HTTP 'Accept' header in client requests?
Options: It informs the server which content/media types (e.g. application/json, text/html) the client is able to understand
It accepts terms of service agreements
It approves server SSL certificates
It passes authentication credentials
Questions.Explanation: The Accept header is used in content negotiation to tell the server which media formats the client prefers.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the standard HTTP status code returned upon successful resource creation?
Options: 201 Created
200 OK
204 No Content
301 Moved Permanently
Questions.Explanation: 201 Created signifies that the request succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource, usually with a Location header.

Questions.QuestionText: How many columns does the Bootstrap responsive grid system divide each row into?
Options: 12 columns
10 columns
16 columns
8 columns
Questions.Explanation: Bootstrap's flexbox grid system is based on a 12-column layout across 6 responsive breakpoints (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, xxl).

Questions.QuestionText: What major change in JavaScript architecture occurred in Bootstrap 5 compared to Bootstrap 4?
Options: Bootstrap 5 dropped jQuery dependency in favor of vanilla JavaScript
Bootstrap 5 requires React or Vue
Bootstrap 5 removed all JavaScript plugins
Bootstrap 5 added Angular CLI requirements
Questions.Explanation: Bootstrap 5 completely eliminated the jQuery dependency, rewriting all plugins in clean vanilla ECMAScript.

Questions.QuestionText: Which Bootstrap 5 utility class provides subtle background and text coloring for alert/badge contrast?
Options: bg-success-subtle and text-success-emphasis
bg-super-green
color-success-light
style-alert-soft
Questions.Explanation: Bootstrap 5.3+ introduced subtle background and emphasis utilities (-subtle and -emphasis) for modern color contrast.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the class 'd-flex justify-content-between align-items-center' do?
Options: Creates a flexbox container with space between items horizontally and centers items vertically
Hides the element on mobile screens
Centers all text in a block element
Creates a 2-column table
Questions.Explanation: d-flex enables flex display, justify-content-between spaces items across main axis, and align-items-center centers along cross axis.

Questions.QuestionText: Which class is used in Bootstrap 5 to create a rounded, card-like elevated panel?
Options: card shadow-sm border rounded-3
panel panel-default
box box-elevated
div-container-card
Questions.Explanation: card combined with shadow-sm and border rounded-3 produces modern, polished container cards.

Questions.QuestionText: Which HTML5 semantic element is best suited to encapsulate content that is tangentially related to the main content (e.g. sidebar)?
Options: <aside>
<section>
<article>
<nav>
Questions.Explanation: <aside> represents a portion of a document whose content is only indirectly related to the document's main content.

Questions.QuestionText: In CSS, what is the effect of 'box-sizing: border-box;'?
Options: The element's padding and border are included in its total specified width and height
The element is given a 3D border shadow
Margin is calculated inside the element border
The element is restricted to square aspect ratios
Questions.Explanation: border-box includes padding and border within the defined width/height, preventing layout overflow issues.

Questions.QuestionText: What CSS feature enables responsive designs that adapt according to screen width or device orientation?
Options: @media queries
@font-face
@keyframes
@import
Questions.Explanation: CSS Media Queries (@media (max-width: ...)) apply styles conditionally based on device capabilities and viewport dimensions.

Questions.QuestionText: Which CSS property defines CSS Custom Properties (CSS variables) that can be inherited across the entire document?
Options: :root { --primary-color: #0F6B5C; }
$primary-color = #0F6B5C;
@var primary-color: #0F6B5C;
#global { primary-color: #0F6B5C; }
Questions.Explanation: Declaring --variable-name on the :root pseudo-class makes the custom property globally accessible via var(--variable-name).

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of the 'aria-label' attribute in HTML?
Options: Provides an accessible text label for screen readers when no visible text is present on an interactive element
Applies a tooltip on hover
Translates text automatically into Arabic
Styles the element font color
Questions.Explanation: aria-label defines an accessible name string for assistive technologies like screen readers.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the difference between 'interface' and 'type' alias in TypeScript?
Options: Interfaces support declaration merging and are extensible with 'extends'; type aliases can define unions, primitives, and mapped types
Interfaces are compiled into JavaScript objects at runtime while types are deleted
Type aliases cannot be used with objects
Interfaces cannot be implemented by classes
Questions.Explanation: Interfaces allow declaration merging and object inheritance, whereas types support unions (A | B), tuples, and advanced type operators.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the 'unknown' type represent in TypeScript compared to 'any'?
Options: 'unknown' is the type-safe counterpart of 'any'; any operation on 'unknown' requires type narrowing or casting first
'unknown' disables all TypeScript type checks completely
'unknown' is identical to 'never'
'unknown' can only store string values
Questions.Explanation: unknown forces the developer to perform type checking (typeof, instanceof) before performing operations, whereas any disables all checks.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the 'readonly' modifier do on object properties in TypeScript?
Options: Prevents reassignment to the property after initialization
Makes the property private to the class
Hides the property from Object.keys()
Deletes the property from compiled JavaScript
Questions.Explanation: readonly ensures compile-time immutability by disallowing reassignment to that property.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of Generics in TypeScript (e.g. <T>)?
Options: Allows creating reusable components and functions that work over a variety of types while preserving type safety
Generates random data for unit tests
Translates TypeScript to C# code
Bypasses strict null checks
Questions.Explanation: Generics provide type variables that capture input types and maintain end-to-end type safety in functions, interfaces, and classes.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the non-null assertion operator '!' do in TypeScript (e.g. user!.name)?
Options: Tells the TypeScript compiler to assert that an expression is neither null nor undefined at compile time
Performs a runtime check and throws an exception if null
Converts the value to a boolean false
Inverts the bitwise representation
Questions.Explanation: The postfix ! operator is a compile-time assertion that removes null and undefined from the type without runtime emission.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary goal of Continuous Integration (CI)?
Options: Automating the building, testing, and validation of code changes merged into a shared repository branch frequently
Manually releasing code once per year
Replacing source control with cloud backups
Automating database backups only
Questions.Explanation: CI ensures developers integrate code frequently, validated by automated builds and tests to detect integration defects early.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the distinction between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
Options: Continuous Delivery automatically prepares tested artifacts ready for release on demand; Continuous Deployment automatically deploys directly to production
Continuous Delivery is for mobile apps; Continuous Deployment is for web apps
Continuous Delivery does not run tests
Continuous Deployment requires manual manager approval for every single build
Questions.Explanation: Continuous Delivery keeps code releasable with manual release trigger; Continuous Deployment automatically deploys passing commits to production.

Questions.QuestionText: In automated pipeline security, where should sensitive credentials (e.g. production connection strings, API keys) be stored?
Options: Encrypted Pipeline Secrets / Key Vaults (never in plain text in repository files or logs)
Hardcoded directly in appsettings.json in the Git repository
Public GitHub environment variables
Committed in a README.md file
Questions.Explanation: Secrets should always be managed in secure key stores and injected into pipeline environments as masked environment variables.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the role of a Quality Gate in a CI pipeline?
Options: Enforcing rules (e.g. all unit tests must pass, zero security vulnerabilities, code coverage thresholds) that block merging if failed
Requiring two developers to type at the same keyboard
Compressing the compiled binaries before saving
Generating user documentation
Questions.Explanation: A Quality Gate defines verifiable criteria that a build must satisfy before proceeding to downstream stages or merging.

Questions.QuestionText: What does a Blue-Green deployment strategy accomplish?
Options: Deploys the new version to an identical idle environment (Green) alongside live (Blue) and switches traffic instantly with zero downtime
Deploys code on Mondays and deletes it on Fridays
Tests code using color-coded user interfaces
Rolls out updates to 10% of servers at a time
Questions.Explanation: Blue-Green deployment runs two identical production environments to enable zero-downtime cutover and instant rollback if issues occur.

Questions.QuestionText: What AWS compute service provides scalable virtual servers in the cloud?
Options: Amazon EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)
Amazon S3
Amazon RDS
AWS Lambda
Questions.Explanation: Amazon EC2 provides resizable virtual machine compute capacity in the AWS cloud.

Questions.QuestionText: Which AWS storage service provides object storage designed for 99.999999999% (11 9's) durability?
Options: Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service)
Amazon EBS
Amazon EFS
Amazon DynamoDB
Questions.Explanation: Amazon S3 stores data as objects within buckets with eleven 9s of durability across multiple Availability Zones.

Questions.QuestionText: What is AWS Lambda?
Options: A serverless compute service that runs code in response to events and automatically manages underlying compute resources
A relational database engine
A domain name registrar
A managed Kubernetes control plane
Questions.Explanation: AWS Lambda is an event-driven, serverless computing platform executing code only when triggered.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of Amazon VPC (Virtual Private Cloud)?
Options: To provision a logically isolated section of the AWS cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a defined virtual network
To host WordPress websites
To provide email marketing services
To monitor application logs
Questions.Explanation: Amazon VPC lets you control your virtual networking environment, including selection of your own IP address range, subnets, and route tables.

Questions.QuestionText: Which service is used in AWS to control identity, access permissions, and roles for users and services?
Options: AWS IAM (Identity and Access Management)
AWS CloudWatch
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Shield
Questions.Explanation: AWS IAM enables you to manage access to AWS services and resources securely using policies and roles.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the smallest deployable computing unit that can be created and managed in Kubernetes?
Options: Pod
Node
Cluster
Deployment
Questions.Explanation: A Pod encapsulates one or more containers, storage resources, and unique network IP address as the basic execution unit in Kubernetes.

Questions.QuestionText: What Kubernetes resource provides a stable network endpoint (virtual IP and DNS name) to expose a group of Pods?
Options: Service
ConfigMap
Volume
DaemonSet
Questions.Explanation: A Kubernetes Service defines a logical set of Pods and a policy by which to access them with load balancing.

Questions.QuestionText: What does a Kubernetes Deployment controller manage?
Options: Declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets, ensuring the desired number of pod replicas are running
Node operating system updates
External domain DNS registration
Docker daemon installation on worker nodes
Questions.Explanation: A Deployment provides declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets, enabling automated rollouts and rollbacks.

Questions.QuestionText: Which component in the Kubernetes Control Plane is responsible for distributing workloads across worker nodes?
Options: kube-scheduler
kube-proxy
kubelet
etcd
Questions.Explanation: The kube-scheduler watches for newly created Pods with no assigned node, and selects an optimal node for them to run on.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the function of 'etcd' in a Kubernetes cluster?
Options: A consistent, highly-available key-value store used as Kubernetes' backing store for all cluster data
A container runtime engine
A web dashboard for developers
A load balancer for external HTTP traffic
Questions.Explanation: etcd stores the complete state and configuration of the Kubernetes cluster.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the difference between 'git fetch' and 'git pull'?
Options: 'git fetch' downloads new remote commits without merging them into your local branch; 'git pull' fetches and automatically merges
'git fetch' deletes local branches while 'git pull' restores them
'git pull' only works on the main branch
There is no difference
Questions.Explanation: git fetch retrieves updates from the remote repository without altering your working tree; git pull is fetch followed by merge (or rebase).

Questions.QuestionText: What does 'git rebase' do compared to 'git merge'?
Options: 'git rebase' reapplies commits on top of another base tip, creating a linear history; 'git merge' creates a 2-parent merge commit
'git rebase' deletes all commit history permanently
'git merge' requires an internet connection while rebase does not
'git rebase' is only allowed on production servers
Questions.Explanation: Rebasing rewrites commit history by transplanting branch commits sequentially on top of the target branch.

Questions.QuestionText: What does the command 'git reset --soft HEAD~1' do?
Options: Undoes the last commit, leaving all modified changes staged in the index
Completely deletes the commit and discards all file modifications
Pushes the commit to the remote repository
Creates a new tag on the previous commit
Questions.Explanation: --soft moves HEAD back one commit while keeping your working tree changes staged in the index.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the purpose of a .gitignore file?
Options: Specifies intentionally untracked files and patterns that Git should ignore (e.g. bin/, obj/, user secrets, node_modules/)
Ignores Git error messages in the terminal
Deletes files from the remote server on pull
Prevents other developers from editing files
Questions.Explanation: .gitignore tells Git which local build artifacts, logs, and sensitive files to exclude from version tracking.

Questions.QuestionText: What does 'git cherry-pick <commit-hash>' do?
Options: Applies the changes introduced by an existing individual commit onto the currently checked-out branch
Deletes a commit from history
Renames a branch
Creates a fork of the repository
Questions.Explanation: git cherry-pick selects a specific commit by its SHA hash and records its changes as a new commit on the current branch.

Questions.QuestionText: When writing an architectural decision record (ADR), what is the most important element to document?
Options: The context, options considered, trade-offs, and rationale behind the chosen decision
Only the names of the engineers who agreed
The exact cost of developer laptop hardware
Marketing copy for the website
Questions.Explanation: An ADR captures the architectural context, decision, consequences, and trade-offs for future maintainers.

Questions.QuestionText: What constitutes an effective Pull Request description?
Options: A clear summary of what changed, why it changed, how it was tested, and references to related issues
Leaving the description completely blank
Pasting raw binary machine code
Only saying 'fixed stuff'
Questions.Explanation: Clear PR descriptions accelerate code reviews by providing background, rationales, test verification steps, and issue links.

Questions.QuestionText: In asynchronous engineering communication, what is the best practice for reporting bugs?
Options: Provide exact steps to reproduce, expected vs actual behavior, environment details, and logs/screenshots
Say 'the system is broken' without details
Call the on-call engineer at midnight without filing a ticket
Delete the database
Questions.Explanation: Reproduction steps, expected vs actual results, and logs enable rapid isolation and triage.

Questions.QuestionText: Why are diagrams (e.g. C4 model, UML Sequence Diagrams) valuable in system documentation?
Options: They provide visual clarity on system boundaries, component interactions, and data flow
They replace the need for writing source code
They compile directly into SQL tables
They prevent software bugs automatically
Questions.Explanation: Diagrams distill complex distributed relationships into clear visual models accessible across engineering disciplines.

Questions.QuestionText: What does Conventional Commits specification (e.g. 'feat:', 'fix:', 'docs:') provide?
Options: A standardized commit message structure that enables automated changelog generation and clear versioning
An encryption method for Git commits
A syntax requirement enforced by the C# compiler
A way to speed up network downloads
Questions.Explanation: Conventional Commits standardize message formats to convey semantic intent and enable automated tooling.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary objective of a constructive Code Review?
Options: To improve code quality, share knowledge across the team, and catch potential defects collaboratively
To criticize the author personally
To delay feature delivery as long as possible
To rewrite everything in your personal favorite style
Questions.Explanation: Constructive code reviews foster mentorship, improve maintainability, and ensure standard adherence.

Questions.QuestionText: What is a Blameless Post-Mortem in engineering culture?
Options: An incident review focusing on systemic failures, process gaps, and preventative measures rather than blaming individuals
A meeting where the developer responsible for a bug is fired
Ignoring production outages completely
A secret meeting with executives only
Questions.Explanation: Blameless post-mortems analyze root causes to build resilience into systems and processes without assigning personal blame.

Questions.QuestionText: In cross-functional teams, what is the role of empathy in technical collaboration?
Options: Understanding the constraints and priorities of design, product, and QA partners to build better solutions together
Agreeing with every suggestion without evaluating technical feasibility
Avoiding all code discussions
Delegating all coding tasks to junior developers
Questions.Explanation: Cross-functional empathy aligns technical feasibility with user experience and business outcomes.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the best way to handle technical disagreements during architecture design?
Options: Evaluate trade-offs using objective benchmarks, prototype small spikes, and align on team goals
Refuse to work on the project until your design is chosen
Let whoever speaks loudest decide
Flip a coin
Questions.Explanation: Objective criteria, risk analysis, and rapid prototyping resolve architecture debates constructively.

Questions.QuestionText: What does Psychological Safety foster in high-performing engineering teams?
Options: An environment where team members feel safe to ask questions, admit mistakes, and propose innovative ideas without fear of humiliation
A guarantee that no code will ever have bugs
Eliminating code reviews and tests
Working in isolation without team meetings
Questions.Explanation: Psychological safety encourages transparency, rapid learning, and collaborative problem-solving.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the First Principles thinking approach in software engineering?
Options: Breaking a complex problem down to its most fundamental truths and building up a solution from there
Copying and pasting the top answer from StackOverflow
Rewriting the whole system in assembly language
Asking someone else to solve the problem
Questions.Explanation: First principles thinking decomposes problems to foundational truths, avoiding legacy assumptions.

Questions.QuestionText: When debugging a production performance degradation, what should be the first step?
Options: Inspect metrics, telemetry, and profiling data to formulate a hypothesis based on evidence before altering code
Randomly change configuration settings on live servers
Restart all database clusters without checking logs
Immediately rewrite the entire backend
Questions.Explanation: Systematic debugging requires gathering telemetry and metrics to identify the bottleneck before taking action.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the Divide and Conquer strategy in algorithm design (e.g. Merge Sort, Binary Search)?
Options: Dividing a problem into smaller subproblems, solving the subproblems recursively, and combining the results
Splitting a team into competing groups
Deleting half the database records
Running two different operating systems
Questions.Explanation: Divide and conquer recursively breaks problems down into manageable independent subproblems.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the Five Whys technique in root cause analysis?
Options: Iteratively asking 'Why?' five times to peel away symptom layers and reach the underlying systemic cause
Asking five different people for their opinion
Retrying a failed network request five times
Writing five unit tests per class
Questions.Explanation: The Five Whys technique drills down into the causal chain of an issue to determine its foundational defect.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the benefit of defining Minimal Reproducible Examples (MRE) when encountering bugs?
Options: It isolates the exact variable causing the bug, removing unrelated complexity and speeding up fixes
It increases code lines for developer metrics
It replaces integration testing
It requires writing code without an IDE
Questions.Explanation: A Minimal Reproducible Example eliminates noise and proves precisely what triggers the unexpected behavior.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the primary purpose of the Daily Standup (Scrum)?
Options: A 15-minute sync for developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and flag blockers
A detailed performance evaluation of each employee
A time to write code together
A meeting to plan next quarter's roadmap
Questions.Explanation: Daily standups synchronize progress, align on daily commitments, and identify impediments.

Questions.QuestionText: What is the Definition of Done (DoD) in Scrum?
Options: A shared formal agreement of all quality standards and criteria that a product backlog item must meet to be considered completed
When the developer finishes typing code on their local machine
When the sprint deadline is reached regardless of test results
When a customer asks for a new feature
Questions.Explanation: Definition of Done ensures transparency by guaranteeing all completed increments meet quality and testing standards.

Questions.QuestionText: What happens during a Sprint Retrospective meeting?
Options: The team reflects on what went well, what went wrong, and commits to actionable improvements for the next sprint
The team showcases completed features to stakeholders
The Product Owner estimates story points
Developers fix bugs in production
Questions.Explanation: Retrospectives provide continuous process improvement by analyzing team workflow, communication, and tools.

Questions.QuestionText: Who is primarily responsible for maximizing the value of the product and managing the Product Backlog in Scrum?
Options: Product Owner
Scrum Master
Lead Developer
Database Administrator
Questions.Explanation: The Product Owner orders and clarifies backlog items to maximize the business value delivered by the team.

Questions.QuestionText: What is a Story Point in Agile estimation?
Options: A relative unit of measure assessing the combined effort, complexity, and uncertainty of implementing a user story
The exact number of hours an engineer must work
A monetary bonus given for completing a ticket
A count of bug fixes in a release
Questions.Explanation: Story points gauge relative complexity, effort, and risk rather than absolute calendar hours.
